root.label: Associative and unordered
root.note: Sorted trees driven by a comparator versus hash tables driven by hash and equality.

children.label: Ordered containers
children.note: set, map and multi versions are sorted, node based and logarithmic.

children.label: Strict weak ordering
children.note: Compare must make comp(x, x) false; a violation such as less_equal is undefined behavior.

children.label: Equivalence not equality
children.note: Two keys are the same key when neither compares less than the other.

children.label: Range queries
children.note: lower_bound, upper_bound and equal_range exploit the sort order.

children.label: Unordered containers
children.note: Hash tables: constant average cost, linear worst case, unspecified order.

children.label: Buckets and load factor
children.note: Load factor is size over bucket count; max_load_factor defaults to 1.0.

children.label: Rehash
children.note: Growing the bucket count redistributes elements and invalidates iterators, not references.

children.label: reserve(n)
children.note: Equals rehash(ceil(n / max_load_factor())); it avoids rehashing up to n elements.

children.label: Keys and hashing
children.note: Rules the container cannot check for you.

children.label: Const keys
children.note: The element type is pair<const K, V>, because changing a key would break the structure.

children.label: Equal keys, equal hashes
children.note: If the equality predicate holds, the hashes must match, or behavior is undefined.

children.label: Specializing std::hash
children.note: Allowed for your own types; std::hash has no pair or tuple specialization.

children.label: Insertion functions
children.note: They differ in overwrite behavior and in when they construct.

children.label: operator[]
children.note: Inserts a value-initialized element if missing; needs a default constructor; absent on const maps.

children.label: at and find
children.note: at throws std::out_of_range for a missing key; find returns end and changes nothing.

children.label: insert and emplace
children.note: Never overwrite; emplace may build a node before discovering the key exists.

children.label: try_emplace
children.note: C++17: leaves its arguments untouched when the key already exists.

children.label: insert_or_assign
children.note: C++17: always ends with the new value and needs no default constructor.

children.label: Multi containers
children.note: Equivalent keys are allowed.

children.label: Insertion order kept
children.note: A new element goes at the upper end of its equivalent range.

children.label: erase(key)
children.note: Removes every equivalent element and returns the count; erase by iterator removes one.

children.label: No operator[] or at
children.note: A key may map to several values, so key-based access is not offered.

children.label: Stability and choice
children.note: Node storage gives stable addresses; choose by needs.

children.label: Stable addresses
children.note: Elements never move while in the container, so references and pointers survive insertion.

children.label: contains
children.note: C++20 membership test returning bool on all eight containers.
